title: The Tale of Igor's Campaign
summary: An anonymous late twelfth-century poem about Prince Igor of Novhorod-Siverskyi's unsuccessful 1185 campaign against the Cumans. Its manuscript was found in 1795 in the archives of the Transfiguration Monastery in Yaroslavl, published in 1800 and lost in the Moscow fire of 1812. It is a major work of medieval Eastern Slavic literature and urges unity among rulers.

uncertainty.note: The campaign is dated 1185; composition is 'late 12th century' (Encyclopedia of Ukraine), ca. 1188-1200 (Columbia). Pritsak's proposed 1202 is noted by the Encyclopedia as not universally accepted and is excluded.

as_recorded.value: Spring 1185 campaign; poem written in the late 12th century
Igor's army was defeated on May 12, 1185; the page dates the work to about 1188-1200 CE
